data.name: Amrut
data.gender_notes: Amrut is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, the divine elixir of immortality, Amrita, is referred to as Amrut. It is a symbol of purity, devotion, and the quest for eternal life. The name Amrut carries the meaning “Nectar of immortality” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amrut usually hope their child will grow to embody nectar of immortality and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sips from the divine cup of Amrut, granting spiritual enlightenment and eternal life.
data.etymology: Amrut belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Nectar of immortality.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amrut total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu mythology, the sacred drink, Amrita, is mentioned in various epics and scriptures as the divine elixir of immortality. It is believed that Amrita was churned out of the ocean of milk, Sudarshan, by the gods during the Samudra Manthan process. The gods and demons both craved for this nectar, as they believed it would make them immortal. After many battles and struggles, the gods finally managed to acquire the Amrita, and as they were about to take their first sip, the false god Mohini, disguised as a female devil, distracted them and Moon God, Chandra, sneaked in and drank the elixir, becoming immortal in the process. Thus, Amrita represents the pursuit of eternal life, strength, and prosperity.
data.spiritual_significance: Amrut, as a name, is deeply rooted in spirituality and denotes purity and devotion. As per Hindu beliefs, the very name Amrut invokes the blessings of eternal life, wisdom, and prosperity. It symbolizes the timeless intention of the seeker to connect with the divine and attain the bliss of enlightenment. Thus, the name Amrut is a constant reminder of the inner quest for self-realization and the outer pursuit of Dharma, Artha, Kama, and Moksha. Additionally, it is a reminder of the divine elixir that initially endowed immortality to the gods and, later, to the great sages and philosophers, who have, through their dedicated pursuit of spiritual wisdom, attained an immortal status in the annals of human civilization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Amrut symbolizes the divine nectar of immortality and blessings from the gods. It represents the pure, intoxicating essence of life, inspiring joy, happiness, and longevity.

historical_references.reference: The god Amrutas or Amrutasya is mentioned in the Hindu scripture Mahabharata, where he is described as the god of nectar or immortality. He is also known as the god of the river Saraswati.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic that forms a major part of the Hindu mythology.

historical_references.reference: Amrut is also mentioned in the Rigveda, one of the oldest texts in the Indian subcontinent. In the Rigveda, Amrut is described as the divine nectar or the elixir of life that was churned from the ocean of milk (Samudra Manthan) by the gods and demons to obtain immortality.
historical_references.context: Rigveda is a collection of ancient hymns and religious verses, considered sacred in Hinduism.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern usage, the Hindu name 'Amrut' (meaning 'nectar of the gods') is increasingly seen on various platforms due to its association with spirituality, wellness, and beverages. On Instagram, it's used in hashtags for spiritual and wellness accounts. On Pinterest, users pin images of Ayurvedic elixirs and traditional Indian beverages, often referred to as 'Amrut'. Blogs and websites focus on the significance of Amrut in Hindu mythology and its incorporation into modern wellness practices, such as adding Amrut to tea or using it in meditation rituals.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Maya Amrut in Chennai, India attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Amrut, which means "Nectar of immortality". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
